coachingPoints: Teach drop-step and jump-hook footwork before any advanced post move.
Measure rim protection by shots altered, not just blocks — staying down matters.
Build passing from the post and the short roll; double teams punish selfish bigs.
Condition the big to sprint the floor — rim-running beats jogging every time.
commonMistakes: Bringing the ball down low where guards can strip it — keep it high.
Jumping at every shot fake instead of staying grounded.
Camping in the paint on offense for three seconds.
Setting lazy screens and slipping before making contact.
description: Center development: rim protection, rebounding, post scoring, screening and the modern big's passing and shooting.
gameSituations: Drop coverage — containing the ball handler while protecting the rim.
Post double team — reading the help and kicking to the open shooter.
Offensive rebound — tipping or dunking the putback.
Late game — protecting the rim without fouling on the final possession.

howTo.detail: Own the paint on defense: stay between your player and the basket, contest shots vertically with arms straight up, and communicate every screen and cut. The center is the defense's quarterback.
howTo.title: Protect the rim

howTo.detail: Box out with contact, pursue with two hands, and secure the ball at chin level. Then outlet immediately — a quick, accurate outlet pass starts the fast break.
howTo.title: Rebound and outlet

howTo.detail: Seal deep with a wide base, catch with two hands, and score with the drop step, jump hook, and up-and-under. Keep the ball high and make your move in two dribbles or fewer.
howTo.title: Score in the post

howTo.detail: Sprint rim-to-rim in transition — the first big down the floor gets dunks and deep seals. In the half court, set hard screens and roll with purpose.
howTo.title: Run and screen

howTo.detail: Modern centers must pass: hit cutters from the high post, find shooters when doubled, and make short-roll reads. Add a reliable jumper and, eventually, three-point range to pull defenders out.
howTo.title: Pass and stretch

howTo.detail: Call out screens ('screen left!'), direct rotations, and organize the defense. The center sees the whole floor — use that voice every possession.
howTo.title: Talk and organize

title: Center Development
whatIsIt: The center — the '5' — is the team's anchor: protecting the rim, rebounding, scoring inside, setting screens, and organizing the defense. Traditionally the tallest player, the center lives near the basket on both ends.

The position has evolved dramatically. Modern centers still protect the rim and rebound, but many now shoot threes, handle the ball in the open floor, and pass like guards. The job description keeps expanding — which makes skilled bigs more valuable than ever.
whyItMatters: Rim protection and rebounding are the two most reliable ways to control a game. A dominant center deters drives, ends opponent possessions, and creates second chances on offense. Even as the game spreads out, teams with a real anchor at the '5' defend the most valuable real estate on the court — the paint.
